I'm a lawyer and I'm a little ticked because this isn't the best cause of action that could have been filed. There was a better cause of action to file, and I had some correspondence with Trump's lawyers to help flesh it out for them, at their request. They should have sued as a class action on behalf of all consumers of the NYT (both in print and online) under the Consumer Protection Act, alleging that the NYT had misrepresented its product to its consumers when they knew it was untrue. Under the CPA, the NYT would have to pay damages to tens of millions of readers, tripled the damages, and paid all attorneys fees and costs of the suit. And the precedential value of the lawsuit would require the NYT to append each story with a disclaimer that "parts of the following article are the conclusions of the writer and are not supported by fact or critical investigation."
